text:
Marina: Heads-up — we started seeing a regression in token-level latencies on /v1/generate around 12:02 UTC. P50 is stable but P90/P99 for the first 10 tokens jumped ~40-60ms for model-x-quant on dedicated clusters.
Ashok: Ugh. Any recent changes to kernel selection or batching heuristics? :eyes:
Marina: yep — merged a kernel-selector tweak last night (PR #4021) that prefers fused-kernel A for medium-length sequences. It improved throughput on our perf bench but might be suboptimal for short chat-style sequences.
Sasha: can we surface which tokens are hot? token 1 vs tail? We should confirm whether the spike is head tokens (prompt prep) or autoreg generation.
Marina: quick profile dump attached (snippet):
```
profile: model-x-quant
tokens 1-5: avg 22ms -> 68ms
tokens 6-50: avg 9ms -> 12ms
kv_cache_hit_rate: 82% -> 60% on route: /v1/generate
```
Eva: KV cache hit-rate drop is suspicious. I deployed a change to eviction TTL in the same window — might be two interacting regressions.
Henry: so two levers: kernel choice + KV behavior. Which one correlates with the P90 jump? Marina: token-1 latency jump aligns with the kernel selector flip, token 2-5 correlates more with KV misses.
Ashok: plan: (1) revert kernel selector for model-x-quant on dedicated canary, (2) force KV TTL back to previous value in canary, (3) add token-level SLI on dashboards. Can we do the revert ASAP?
deploy-bot: deploy finished: canary-revert-kernel @ 1764001345 by Henry — status: success
Henry: I pushed the revert to canary, rolling 10% of traffic now.
Sasha: adding two graphs to the perf dashboard: token latency heatmap (tokens 1-50) and per-route KV hit-rate. Will also add p90/p99 per route. ETA 20m.
Eva: I rolled the TTL back on canary at 12:11 UTC. Observability note: KV hits returned to ~80% on canary.
Marina: after reverting kernel and TTL on canary: P90 for head tokens back within 10ms of baseline. Full rollout pending once we validate 30m steady.
oncall-bot: alert triggered: route /v1/generate P99 token latency > 180ms (occurrence: 1). Severity: info. Paging threshold not met.
Ashok: good catch. Next steps: (a) run perf profile across seq-len distribution and generate a kernel selection matrix, (b) update batching heuristic to bias small-batch fast-path for short sequences, (c) add automated alerts for token-level burn-rate (if p99 rises > 2x baseline for 10m).
Sasha: re: alerts — I'll add an anomaly detector that looks at token-level residuals, plus a burn-rate alert for p99. We'll wire paging only for sustained >3x for 15m to avoid noise.
Marina: can someone run the seq-distribution job on prod traces for last 24h? I want to verify how much traffic is short-chat.
Henry: running now — ETA 6m.
Henry: results: 68% of requests have max_seq_len <= 64. So short sequences are the majority on this route.
Eva: that explains why kernel A (optimized for medium-long) regressed customer-visible latency despite better aggregate throughput.
Ashok: decision: keep revert in prod, then implement kernel-selection that uses seq_len histogram + cost-model. Also, make batching heuristic respect a per-route "prefer-small-batch" flag.
Sasha: filing a postmortem ticket with action items: update kernel selector cost model, upgrade KV eviction telemetry, add token-level SLIs & burn-rate alert, and add a canary checklist for kernel changes. Ticket #INF-1128.
Marina: thanks everyone. Quick wins: dashboards + short-seq bias in batching. Longer: kernel cost model and rolling perf tests in CI.
Eva: noted — I'll follow up on KV telemetry changes and attach TTL metrics to per-route dashboards.
Ashok: assign owners and let's track in the eng-runtime board. :thumbsup:
Marina: adding follow-up meeting at 14:00 UTC to review canary metrics and rollout cadence.
